video_title: Blazers Leaving Portland Becoming More Likely?

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Deteriorating relationship between the Blazers and city officials
quotes.excerpt: the rhetoric between the politicians and the Blazers organization is deteriorating

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: There is a story written by Bill Oram of the Portland Oregonian about the Blazers situation, which is getting worse by the day. The rhetoric between the politicians and the Blazers organization is deteriorating. Bill Oram got a hold of what he calls a top Blazers official. I don't know what that means, but the freedom with which this individual speaks is with the kind of thrust that leads you to believe it's a very, very high Blazers official, and that it was certainly with the full blessing of Tom Dunden.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim McMahon
text_blocks.text: And it was certainly with the full blessing of Tom Dunden.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Portland Blazers board of directors meeting could signal major conflict
quotes.excerpt: it could be the declaration of all-out war

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: On Monday, the Blazers board of directors, which is essentially their owners, have a meeting. I have no idea what's going to come out of that meeting, but it could be the declaration of all-out war. This is a response to the city sending the Blazers what they wanted in the lease. They want the Blazers to sign a lease to get the money to renovate their arena.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: They don't like it. He expressed the opposite of support for the idea that they would have to use unionized labor.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Blazers official criticizes city's lack of appreciation for the deal
quotes.excerpt: The city of Portland doesn't even recognize they got a sweetheart deal

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Further quotes: The city of Portland doesn't even recognize they got a sweetheart deal and they're making it complicated. And if they want to say no, if they don't want us, then that's fine.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Blazers official claims relocation would not result in financial loss
quotes.excerpt: It might be okay to spend a billion dollars on a relocation fee if the value doubles

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: It's not like we lose money moving the team, the team official said. We might spend money, but we won't lose money. It might be okay to spend a billion dollars on a relocation fee if the value of the team doubles. Of course you would do that.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim McMahon
text_blocks.text: And isn't there something in there about them not having a jersey sponsor being the only team?

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Blazers' broadcast crew changes and Kevin Calabro's departure
quotes.excerpt: Kevin Calabro, who's been with them for 10 years, was the voice of the Sonics

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Their broadcast crew, a lot of whom had been there for a lot of years, they let the radio voices go. Kevin Calabro, who's been with them for 10 years, was the voice of the Sonics. The Sonics moved, he became an ESPN broadcaster. He actually left ESPN because he wanted to call games for a team again. And with the Blazers job came open, and I remember talking to him when he left, he was like, yeah, this is a tough decision, but I love being the voice of a team and I'm going to go do it.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim McMahon
text_blocks.text: Now, why would he say subprime, Windy?

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Tom Dunden's reputation for subprime auto loans
quotes.excerpt: Tom Dunden was known for giving subprime auto loans

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Because Tom Dunden was known for giving subprime auto loans. That's one of his businesses.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim McMahon
text_blocks.text: This guy has a way with words. Our guy Tom Haberstrow, his contract wasn't renewed.
